findings.problem: The same argument is written out twice in one proof, once for `fun i : Fin 7 => B.b i.succ` (hrange, lines 199–210) and once for `B.twD7Quot.b` (hrange7, lines 261–271). Each time it states `Set.range f = insert (f 0) (Set.range fun j => f j.succ)`. Each time it proves a `Fin.tail … = …` equation by `funext j; rfl`, rewrites with `Fin.range_fin_succ`, and then feeds the result into `closure_insert_eq_sup`. This is about 12 lines of boilerplate repeated, apart from the extra `Fin.succ_zero_eq_one'` fix-up in the first copy. Both blocks exist only to prove the same fact, that the closure of a Fin (n+1)-indexed family is `zpowers (f 0) ⊔ closure (tail)`. That fact is stated in a form bound to this one proof instead of as a reusable lemma.
findings.proposed_change: Next to `closure_insert_eq_sup`, add a private lemma: `private theorem closure_range_fin_succ_eq_sup {G : Type*} [Group G] {n : ℕ} (f : Fin (n+1) → G) : Subgroup.closure (Set.range f) = Subgroup.zpowers (f 0) ⊔ Subgroup.closure (Set.range fun j : Fin n => f j.succ)`. Proof sketch: `rw [Fin.range_fin_succ, closure_insert_eq_sup]` then close with `rfl`, since `Fin.tail f` unfolds to `fun j => f j.succ`. Then rewrite `hA1` as `rw [hA, show (B.dropFirst).span = Subgroup.closure (Set.range fun i : Fin 7 => B.b i.succ) from rfl, closure_range_fin_succ_eq_sup (fun i : Fin 7 => B.b i.succ)]`, with a `Fin.succ_zero_eq_one'` rewrite for the `0`-th term. Rewrite `hEbar_sup` as `change Subgroup.closure (Set.range B.twD7Quot.b) = _; rw [closure_range_fin_succ_eq_sup B.twD7Quot.b, himgT]`. After this, `hrange`, `hrange7` and both `htail`/`hfun` blocks can be deleted. `closure_insert_eq_sup` could be inlined into the new lemma or kept.
findings.benefit: The two copies of the tail-range bookkeeping are replaced by one short proved lemma. `hA1` and `hEbar_sup` then read as direct applications of it. The long `canonPosition_twD7Quot` proof gets about 20 lines shorter. Any change to how the basis is split into head and tail only has to be made in one place.
